full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in-short, are that the present appellants as plaintiffs instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 23 of 1978 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal imp leading the defendants for declaration of title on the averments that one Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was owner of the suit land appertaining to CS Dag Nos.1194 and 1195 of Mouza Charvaduria measuring about 17.33 acres of land, who took settlement by executing a registered kabuliyat in favour of the then Government on 7-11-21. At the time of taking settlement of the suit land Abdul Kader Mia was a seasonal but collector of khash mohal; that Abdul Kader Mia died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs while he was in service; that Abdul Kader Mia in connection with his service posted different station in which he assigned his full brother defendant No. 2 to look after the suit property; that the defendant No.  2 with ill motive got the suit land recorded in the name of the defendant Nos.1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia in equal share, that is, 3 arenas 4 gandas share; that the preparation of RS Khatian in the name of defendant Nos. 1-4 and Abdul Kader Mia was collusive and without any legal basis; that on the basis of wrong RS Khatian, the SA Khatian has also been pre-pared wrongly in the name of the defendants and Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land in which the defendant Nos. 1-4, in-fact, have no right, title or legal interest whatsoever; that Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was the exclusive owner of the suit land, who used to possess the suit land through different bargadars on the basis of barga Kabuliyats and after the death of Abdul Kader Mia, the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land through different bargadars on payment of rent to the Government; that the plaintiffs demanded Nadabinama or Multiparty in respect of the suit land in which the defendants Nos.1-4 have not tile or interest whatsoever but the defendant Nos.1-4 refused to execute any Nadabi  Muktipatra in their favour in respect of the suit land on 27th poush, 1384 BS; that the preparation of the wrong record of rights have cast a cloud upon the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land and hence, the suit for declaration of title. 

 8. Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-appellants in the course of his argument has taken us through the impugned judgment and decree, deposition of witnesses, exhibits and other materials on record and then submits that the findings of the trial Court below that Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs had no source of income at the time of execution of kabuliyat dated 7-11-21 (Exhibit l) while he was a school going boy, his father Abdul Latif Mia took settlement of the suit land in the benami of his eldest son Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs is perverse being contrary to the material evidence on record. He next submits that the trial Court below having failed to consider the vital aspects of the case that Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs took settlement of the suit land from the then government on 7-11-21 and he executed and registered Kabuliyat in favour of landlord on 7-11-1921 and to prove the case the original Kabulyat was called for from the collector ate on 11-8-1979 vide order No. 27, Kabulyat was exhibited as Exhibit 1 and the settlement was acted upon vide Exhibit Nos. 1A-1G that is the chronological registered barga kabulyat which were given by abraders in favour of Abdul Kader Mia and in those deeds including Exhibit 1 the occupation of Abdul Kader has been consistently stated as service holder. He further submits that the trial Court without assigning any sound reason most illegally ignored all registered documents (exhibits "1 and 1A-1G series") which were produced from the custody of the plaintiffs and those documents are more than 30 years old documents and have strong presumptive value as per provision of section 90 of the Evidence Act. 

 11. Mr Nurul Amin while elaborating his submissions referred to the registered deeds including registered kabuliyat dated 7-114961 and argued that Abdul Kader Mia was in service at the time of execution of kabulyat dated 7-11-1961 and if Abdul Kader Mia found to be minor he could not be allowed to execute and register the kabuliyat on 7-11-21 in favour of the Government but the trial Court below being misdirected itself most illegally on the basis of un-corroborative testimony of the DWs held that at the time of settlement Abdul Kader was minor and Abdul Latif Mia took settlement in the benami of his minor son Abdul Kader Mia. He further submits that admittedly Abdul Kader himself executed and registered kabuliyat on 7-11-21 (Exhibit 1) and several deeds were executed in favour of Abdul Kader (Exhibit 1A to 1G series) wherein his occupation has been consistently stated as service holder, these registered documents were not considered by the trial Judge and he simply relied only on service book of Abdul Kader Mia and held that Abdul Kader Mia was minor at the time of execution of kabuliyat on 7-11-21, this finding of the trial Court below is illegal, which clearly contradicts the old registered documents. Mr Md Nurul Amin, to fortify his submission has relied on the decisions reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76, 44 DLR (AD) 162, 39 DLR (AD) 78, Abdul Hafez vs Lal Meah 1988 BLD 497 = 38 DLR 327, 6 MLR (AD) 49, AIR 1928 (Madras) 14, Sontosh Kumar Deb vs Hiron Chandra Day 1995 BLD 221, Janab Ali Mondal vs Md Anowar Hossain 2004 BLD 243, 2003 BLD (AD) 82, 7 BLT 133, 35 DLR (AD) 216, 43 DLR (AD) 55 and Md Shamsul Huda vs Bangladesh 2000 BLD (AD) 48 = 5 BLC (AD) 108. 

 12. Mr Md Nurul Amin, finally relying on the decision reported in 1 XP (AD) 73 submits that the original title deed is in the name of, Abdul Kader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiff-appellants and on the basis of that registered kabuliyat PS record was prepared in the name of Abdul Kader Mia but subsequently SA and RS record was prepared in the name of the defendants and in such situation the conflicting between kabala and khatian the earlier registered kabuliyat prevails over the subsequent record of rights in RS khatian and SA khatian. 

 17. It is found that during trial the kabuliyat was proved as Exhibit 1, both the parties at the trial in their respective evidence admitted that kabuliyat dated 7-11-1921 (Exhibit 1) is a registered document. The contesting defendant No. 2, in his written statement stated as follows: 

 18. On perusal of the kabuliyat dated 7-11-1921 (Exhibit 1), it appears that there is a precondition inserted into it that no one can take such settlement in the benami of others. In this connection a portion of the kabuliyat dated 7-11-1921 (Exhibit 1) is reproduced hereunder: 

 19. From the above, it transpires that Exhibit 1, kabuliyat dated 7-11-21 is admittedly a registered document. The sole contesting defendant No. 2, (DW-2) claimed his title by virtue of said kabuliyat. During the trial no dispute was raised in the trial Court as to its registration. 

 20. On perusal of Exhibit 1-G series, it transpires that in those old documents the occupation of Abdul Kader Mia has been consistently stated as service. Mr Azizul Haque, the learned Advocate argues that at the relevant time if Abdul Kader Mia was found to be minor he could not be allowed to execute and register the kabuliyat in favour of the then Government. He also argues that the age of Abdul Kader Mia as mentioned in the service book (exhibit-9) was not correct and in that view of the matter the trial Court below was absolutely wrong in finding that Abdul Cadre Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was minor having no source of income. We find consider-able merit in the above submission of Mr Azizul Haque. 

 24. In consideration of this material evidence on record and facts, our view is there-fore, that the reasons given by the trial Court below for passing the impugned judgment on the point that Abdul Kuader Mia, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was a benamder and the plaintiffs could not prove their exclusive possession over the suit land are not sustainable either in law or on facts. Furthermore, in his connection it may be mentioned that a kabuliyat (Exhibit 1) executed and registered in 1921 creates a presumption that the registration authority under the then British Government was satisfied that the executants Abdul Kader Mia was squarely a valid citizen to execute the kabuliyat (Exhibit 1). 

 28. At the end of the day, Mr Abdul Quayum having himself realied the fate of the case, like a drowning man, tried to catch at straw and accordingly, he has raised 2 points for the first time before this Court that RS and SA khatians "Exhibit 5-5C" are public document and those document highlights that the suit property had been diluviated and as per President's Order Nos. 135 /72 tenants lost their title and the diluviated land vested upon the Government and no Court can pass any decree and in that view of the matter the suit abates and suffers from defect of party in not impleading the government and the exhibit-1 (kabuliyat dated 7-11-1921) is an unregistered document. 

 29. To meet the last branch of argument of Mr Abdul Quayum, we have carefully examined the entire evidence on record and it appears that at the trial both the parties admitted in their respective testimony that Exhibit 1, kabuliyat dated 7-11-1921 executed and registered by Abdul Kader Mia. It also appears that out of 4 defendants only defendant No.  2 (DW 2) Rafiqul Alam alias Rafiqul Islam contested the suit by filing written statement, who in his written statement as well as evidence admitted about the registration of the kabuliyat dated 7-11-1921. 

 30. Upon a scrutiny of the evidence on record, it appears that the Exhibit 1, kabulyat dated 7-11-1921 is admittedly a registered document of 1921, the defendants also claimed their title by virtue of the same kabuliyat (exhibit-1). No dispute was raised in the trial Court as to its registration nor nay finding on this point in the judgment of the Subordinate Judge, Barisal. The records shows that the trial Court called for the original kabuliyat from the Collectoriate. Therefore, we do not find any substance in the last branch of argument of Mr. Abdul Quayum that the kabuliyat (Exhibit 1) is an unregistered document particularly when the same is nobody's case. 

 32. Be that as it may, the records of rights of the Government which at best are evidence of possession at the time when such records are prepared and not an evidence of title. This is a well-established principle of law. A registered kabala is an evidence of title which will prevail over the other records of rights, until and unless such kabala/kabuliyat is cancelled on a specific allegation of fraud by any civil court in an appropriate civil suit.
